newsitem.title: UK: Vickers still cautious despite profits rise.
newsitem.headline: Vickers still cautious despite profits rise.

text.p: Vickers Plc announced an 11 percent rise in annual profits on Wednesday but the Rolls-Royce cars to Challenger tanks manufacturer cautioned that sterling's recent strength clouded the outlook for its export-driven business in 1997.

Pretax profits in 1996 increased to 83.3 million pounds ($132.4 million) on sales up 4.7 percent at 1.97 billion pounds and Vickers said it would pay a final dividend of 4.5 pence, making 7.2 pence for the year, up seven percent in line with an increase in earnings to 16.7p.

"1996 represented a competent performance for the Vickers Group as a whole," chairman Sir Richard Lloyd said in his results statement. "These results were achieved in the context of a demanding investment programme, which saw further substantial expenditure during 1996."

But he added: "Because of the effects on export orders and earnings of the rise in the trade-weighted value of sterling against other currencies which began last autumn, it is unusually difficult to foresee the trends of sales and profits in 1997."
But over the next two years the strategies for each business were now "thoroughly founded," Lloyd said, and so "another better performance should be achieved."
